ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, the input signal vi passes through a coupling capacitor, then a resistor labeled 10 kΩ is connected in series to the transistor base; the transistor emitter is grounded, and the collector is connected to a 13.7 V power supply through a 12 kΩ resistor; from the collector/output node there is a resistor labeled 100 kΩ feeding back to the base; the output vo is taken out from the collector through the right-side coupling capacitor, and the transistor is labeled β=100. Reasoning: According to the approximate method required by the problem, treating the coupling capacitors as AC short circuits, this circuit can be regarded as a common-emitter inverting feedback amplifier with collector-base feedback. The closed-loop voltage gain is approximately the ratio of the feedback resistor to the input resistor and carries a negative sign: Av ≈ -100 kΩ / 10 kΩ = -10. Therefore the magnitude of the voltage gain is |Av| ≈ 10.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses the feedback-amplifier/virtual-ground approximation rather than detailed transistor small-signal parameter calculation; this is the natural single high-level route for the approximate gain.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the circuit as an NPN common-emitter stage: emitter grounded, collector connected to 13.7 V through 12 kΩ, output taken from the collector through a coupling capacitor, input source coupled through a capacitor and then a 10 kΩ resistor into the base, and a 100 kΩ resistor feeding back from collector/output node to the base; β is labeled 100.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to know the requested quantity is the approximate magnitude of the voltage gain A_v, so the sign of the inverting gain is discarded.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: At midband, coupling capacitors are treated as shorts and the DC supply is AC ground. A common-emitter transistor provides inversion and high open-loop gain; with collector-to-base negative feedback and sufficiently large loop gain, the base summing node is approximately an AC virtual ground, so the closed-loop voltage gain is approximately the inverting resistor ratio: A_v ≈ -R_f/R_in.
